question.prompt: A base-\(10\) three-digit number \(n\) is selected at random. Which of the following is closest to the probability that the base-\(9\) representation and the base-\(11\) representation of \(n\) are both three-digit numerals?

solutions.explanation:
A three-digit numeral in base \(b\) starts at \(100_b=b^2\) and ends just before \(1000_b=b^3\). Thus it represents exactly the integers satisfying \(b^2\le n<b^3\).

For base \(9\), this requires
\[
81\le n\le728.
\]
For base \(11\), it requires
\[
121\le n\le1330.
\]
The original choice also satisfies \(100\le n\le999\). All three requirements therefore hold exactly when
\[
121\le n\le728.
\]
Including both endpoints gives \(728-121+1=608\) favorable integers. There are \(999-100+1=900\) equally likely choices in total, so the probability is
\[
\frac{608}{900}\approx0.676.
\]
The closest listed value is \(0.7\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
solutions.title: Find the ranges for three-digit numerals
